title: Raptor Healthcare POC — Performance matrix and workshop notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc summarizes the benchmarking and workshop outcomes for the Raptor Health POC (clinical summarization + triage assistant). The goal: validate latency, throughput, and per-token cost targets for three deployment options (hosted, dedicated GPU pool, private VPC) across representative clinical workloads and to capture tradeoffs for the customer workshop on 2026-11-10.

Background / customer asks (short):
- Raptor Health wants a near-real-time assistant for clinicians: single-turn chart summarization (short), multi-turn patient history synthesis (long), and an intent/triage classifier for routing to specialist queues.
- SLO targets: p50 generation latency <= 250 ms for short prompts, p95 <= 800 ms; for longer summarization p95 <= 2.5s.
- Throughput target: 100 concurrent short requests sustained during peak (bursty), and cost target to be under $0.50 per 1k output tokens on production load.

High-level test matrix executed (workshop tests):
- Models evaluated: open-13b (fp16), open-13b-q4 (4-bit quant), med-7b-quant (medical-tuned 7b q4), and a smaller med-3b (fp16) as a fallback.
- Hardware: Dedicated A100-80GB (single card), Dedicated 2xA100-80GB (multi-card inference with pipeline), Dedicated T4 (for cold path cost sim), Hosted high-tier nodes (Redwood-managed).
- Modes: single-request latency, steady-state throughput (concurrency sweep), KV/prefix cache enabled vs disabled, and large-batch cold-start.
- Workloads: 
  * Short summarization: 50–150 tokens input, 60–120 token output (typical chart snippet -> brief summary).
  * Long synthesis: 800–2,500 tokens input (combined encounter history), 300–800 token output.
  * Triage classifier: short inputs, logits-only reranking flow (embedding + small reranker).
- Measurement windows: 10 minute steady-state runs for each point, repeated 3 times.

Key results (summary numbers, median of runs):
- Short summarization (open-13b-fp16 on single A100-80GB): p50 = 180 ms, p95 = 620 ms, throughput at 100 concurrent sustained = 95 rps (requests per second), tokens/s = ~18k output tokens/s.
- Short summarization (open-13b-q4 on single A100-80GB): p50 = 150 ms, p95 = 540 ms, throughput at 100 concurrent = 115 rps, tokens/s = ~21k output tokens/s.
- Long synthesis (open-13b-fp16, single A100): p50 = 1.1 s, p95 = 2.6 s (slightly above target), sustained concurrency 20 -> 18 rps.
- Long synthesis (2xA100 with pipeline enabled): p50 = 0.85 s, p95 = 1.9 s, sustained concurrency 40 -> 38 rps.
- Triage classifier (med-3b on T4): classification latency p50 = 80 ms, p95 = 220 ms, throughput = 320 rps (cheap path).

Cost observations (approximation using Redwood pricing simulation for dedicated capacity):
- open-13b-fp16 on single A100 — marginal compute cost approximated at $2.80 per hour, translating to ~ $0.42 per 1k output tokens assuming a steady-state of 18k tokens/s and 24% utilization across day (workload shape adjusted).
- open-13b-q4 reduces effective cost by ~25% in our run (kernel efficiency + smaller memory moves) -> estimated $0.30 per 1k output tokens.
- med-3b on T4 for classifier: negligible token cost (~$0.06 per 1k output tokens) and recommended as routing edge.
- Multi-card pipeline for long synth increases throughput and meets latency SLOs but raises hourly cost ~1.6x; however, per-token cost for long synth drops due to higher concurrency utilization.

Detailed observations and anomalies (notes from runs):
- KV / prefix cache had outsized impact on short summarization p95: enabling prefix cache reduced p95 by ~28% on average for repeated similar patient notes. This suggests caching is a top lever for Raptor where many chart snippets share templates.
- Quantized model (q4) delivered consistent latency wins but occasional 1–2% output token-quality regressions on specific medical abbreviations in our QA checks — recommend targeted eval on critical diagnoses before full rollout.
- Memory pressure on single A100 for open-13b-fp16 with long inputs required L2 memory swaps in one run (we saw +40% tail latency spike). This was mitigated with 2xA100 pipeline and by trimming KV retention during long synth windows.
- Networking: hosted-hosted cross-region tests increased p95 by ~220 ms for short requests. Recommend colocating dedicated nodes in customer-preferred region for production.

Tradeoffs / recommendations for Raptor (practical stack):
1) Hybrid path (recommended initial):
   - Route short summarization and triage to med-3b (T4) and med-7b-q4 respectively for cost-sensitive flows, with KV cache enabled and a lightweight prefix cache TTL of 30s for repeated clinical templates.
   - Route long synthesis to dedicated 2xA100 cluster running open-13b-fp16 with pipeline; enable dynamic autoscale + reserved capacity for peak windows.
   - Fallback policy: if dedicated capacity saturated, fallback to hosted open-13b-q4 (best-effort) to preserve availability.

2) Performance knobs to tune in Phase 1:
   - Prefix/KV cache TTL and shard keys aligned to patient encounter id -> high hit-rate for short use cases.
   - Favor q4 variants for short/medium prompts after medical QA gating; keep fp16 for long synthesis.
   - Configure auto-batching window to 8–12 ms for short requests (balances latency vs tokens throughput).

3) Cost/contract ask for customer procurement:
   - Reserved 2xA100 nodes for long-synth dedicated pool (commit: 1x 2-card pool, monthly) to get discounted hourly and predictable p95.
   - On-demand T4 pool for classifier and short summaries (burstable).

Action items and next steps (workshop owners):
- (Aisha) Run full medical-term QA sweep on open-13b-q4 and med-7b-q4 against Raptor’s 120-case testset by 2026-11-19.
- (Marco) Prepare rollout plan for prefix cache keys + retention policy; deliver config draft for Redwood console by 2026-11-17.
- (Leah) Cost sensitivity analysis for 1x vs 2x A100 commitment tiers and a 12-month vs 3-month commit — due 2026-11-24.
- (Omar) Integrate classifier into edge path and demo end-to-end latency in customer workshop follow-up (target 2026-11-18).

Open questions for customer:
- Will Raptor accept up to 2% permitted model regression on non-critical abbreviations in exchange for a 25% cost saving from q4 quantization? Need explicit sign-off.
- Peak concurrency windows: confirm expected daily peak length (minutes vs hours) — this affects autoscale sizing and reserved commit level.

Appendix (short):
- Representative invocation commands: see linked github scripts (github.com/redwood/solutions/poc-raptor/bench-scripts).
- Raw logs and per-run csvs are uploaded to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-RAPTOR-POC-2026 -> /artifacts/bench-raw).
- Quick checklist for production hardening: model QA, KV key hygiene, region colocation, canary percent for q4 rollout, SLA rollback policy.

Notes from workshop (customer feedback):
- Raptor Ops was encouraged by low short-path latency and saw KV cache as the highest leverage optimization.
- Clinicians emphasized deterministic tail behavior over median latency; they prefer conservative p95 guarantees for triage to avoid missed routing.
- Legal asked about logging retention and PHI controls — follow-up with Security on private-deploy package pricing and KMS integration.

End of doc.
